notes.claim: Fluid pressure increases with depth because of the weight of the fluid above.
With g about 9.8 m/s² and seawater at 1025 kg/m³, a pressure change of 100 dbar corresponds to a depth change of 99.55 m.
Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
The buoyant force comes from the difference in pressure on the top and bottom of an object.
A submerged object feels a buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces (Archimedes' principle).
Fresh water has a density of about 1000 kg/m³: the kilogram was first the mass of 1000 mL (1 L) of water. Added for i5, whose screens use fresh water at 1000 kg/m³.

Pascal's principle: a change in pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is passed on undiminished to every part of it and to its walls, which is how a hydraulic jack multiplies force. Added for i5's jack screens.
Relative density (specific gravity) is the ratio of a thing's density to water's. Added for i5, which gives seawater's as 1.025.
